Compared three approaches for how to compress payload data going into blobs:

| Strategy | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| **(a)** | `snappy(payload)` → blobs → `snappy(blobs)` |
| **(b)** | `payload` → blobs → `snappy(blobs)` |
| **(c)** | `snappy(each_tx)` → blobs → `snappy(blobs)` |

**Results** (ignoring 32/31 blob encoding overhead):

| | Final size | Ratio |
|-|------------|-------|
| (a) | 98,038 | 43.8% |
| (b) | 98,029 | 43.8% |
| (c) | 112,406 | 50.3% |

**Takeaways:**
- **(a) ≈ (b)**: Double-compressing gains nothing — snappy(snappy(x)) ≈ snappy(x)
- **(c) is ~15% worse**: Per-tx compression destroys cross-tx patterns (repeated addresses, similar gas prices, etc.)
